raw.assessment: The incumbent's reversible assembly offers an opportunity to check the ordered arrangement before dispatch, but the supplied observations do not establish that this check reliably detects component errors. Reported shortages and observed short-partition confusion suggest separate completeness and usability problems. The strongest limiting observation is D2-O6: both workers sometimes approach the eight-minute target on repeated simple orders, so uniformly slow insertion is insufficient as an explanation. Mixed-batch delays could reflect switching or layout complexity; the evidence confounds them. D2-O5 also limits a width-only explanation of insertion retries. Complaint counts and ten unpacking observations do not establish pilot success rates.

openings.claim: Does changing layout between successive orders increase selection and checking time independently of compartment count?
openings.delta: Separates transition overhead from the greater work potentially required by complex layouts, rather than attributing mixed-batch delays to either without measurement.
openings.prediction: If switching contributes materially, the same layout will take longer after a different layout than after a matching layout, particularly during selection or checking.
openings.probe: Time selection, insertion, checking and packing separately on comparable orders. Within each worker and layout, compare repeat versus changed-layout transitions, accounting for exterior color. Use only sequencing that preserves accepted specifications and delivery; otherwise use spare-board samples.
assumptions: Enough comparable transitions can be observed within available working time; otherwise the result remains unresolved.

openings.claim: The three-layout diagram leaves the short partition's role ambiguous even when all correct components are supplied; an order-specific placement diagram could improve unaided arrangement.
openings.delta: Distinguishes instruction ambiguity from missing, incorrect or difficult-to-insert components as the cause of customer difficulty.
openings.prediction: With verified identical component sets, participants receiving an order-specific diagram will more often place the short partition correctly without help.
openings.probe: Randomly assign the ten willing participants to the existing or order-specific diagram using matched, verified samples. Record correct unaided arrangement, short-partition errors and insertion failures separately. Treat results as exploratory; measure diagram preparation time and cost before adoption.
assumptions: Diagrams preserve ordered counts, colors, capacity, footprint and reversible joints.
Preparation fits the fixed deadline, 500-unit initial budget and 0.40-unit recurring allowance; this remains unverified.

raw.assessment: Study relationships rather than the organizer as a whole. Neither combined timing nor customer reports establish a cause. These alternatives retain existing parts, dimensions, assortment, reversible joints, accepted counts and colors, and delivery commitments; their benefit and resource fit need testing.

openings.claim: A missing explicit relation between each supplied partition and its destination may explain some reported errors and short-partition confusion.
openings.delta: Represent the ordered layout as partition-to-slot relations. Replace the generic three-layout diagram with an order-specific silhouette showing each partition's length, orientation and destination. Recompose by matching every required partition to a depicted destination, counting repeated shapes separately; use that same mapping for packing and customer placement without changing the parts.
openings.prediction: With contents independently verified complete, the specific diagram reduces short-partition placement errors relative to the current diagram. Unchanged errors would weaken the mapping explanation.
openings.probe: Randomly split the ten participants between diagrams, balancing layouts. Use five of the 15 sample organizers and reset between participants. Record correct unaided arrangement, short-partition errors and completion time. Treat this as screening, not proof of the pilot target; time workshop checking and cost the replacement diagram.
assumptions: A readable diagram can distinguish the relevant destinations.
Replacement printing and preparation fit both cost caps and the fixed schedule.

openings.claim: Relations between consecutive orders may contribute more delay than any individual organizer configuration: switching layouts could increase selection or checking time.
openings.delta: Represent production as order-to-order transitions. Recompose into the same accepted orders by sequencing equal layouts together, keeping an individual count-and-color slip attached throughout. Assembly and packing remain complete for every order.
openings.prediction: Switching layout increases selection or checking time for the same target layout; an insertion-only difference would favor layout difficulty over transition cost.
openings.probe: Use ten remaining samples in five same-target pairs, one following the same layout and one following a different layout. Counterbalance worker and sequence; hold target color constant. Separately time selection, insertion, checking and packing, and audit contents before considering resequencing.
assumptions: Testing fits available working time before the unchanged delivery date.
Per-order slips remain attached so batching does not substitute colors or compartment counts.

openings.claim: Layout switching may delay selection/checking independently of complexity; grouping equal layouts could help.
openings.discriminator: Same-target delays after changed layouts support switching; insertion-only differences favor layout difficulty.
openings.fit: Conditional: attach count/color slips; preserve specifications and deadline.
openings.probe: Use ten samples as five same-target transition pairs; counterbalance workers/sequence, hold color constant. Separately time selection/insertion/checking/packing; audit contents before resequencing.
openings.uncertainty: Mixed batches confound switching/complexity; comparable transitions and working time may be insufficient.

openings.claim: An order-specific partition-to-slot silhouette may reduce short-partition ambiguity and support packing checks.
openings.discriminator: Verified identical contents isolate diagram effects; unchanged errors weaken mapping. Separate insertion failures from missing/incorrect parts.
openings.fit: Conditional: retain parts, footprint, assortment, reversible joints, ordered counts/colors.
openings.probe: Randomly split ten participants between diagrams, balancing layouts; reset five samples. Depict lengths/orientations/destinations and repeated-shape counts; use mapping for packing. Record unaided correctness, short-partition errors, insertion failures and time; measure checking/preparation time and printing cost.
openings.uncertainty: Readability/resource fit unverified; verified-content trials cannot establish packing completeness. Reports and ten participants cannot establish pilot success.

lineage.reason: Retains paired test, sequencing and slips.

post_distill.decision: Screen within 15 samples and available working time. Adoption requires initial cost <=500, added material/order <=0.40 and fixed delivery. Preserve accepted specifications. Pilot must establish >=98% completeness, median <=8 minutes and >=90% unaided arrangement.
